sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: This lesson is about comparing: cheaper than ours, the shortest delivery time, as strong as yours, too big, such a good relationship. Almost all of it is a small change to the describing word.

examples.en: This hotel room is cheaper than ours.
This shop has the shortest delivery time.
examples.translation: it delivers faster than all others

examples.en: This instant coffee is as strong as yours.
This cabin bag is too big.
examples.translation: it is a problem, it will not fit

examples.en: We have such a good relationship.

blocks.text: To say one thing has more of a quality, add -er to the describing word and use than: cheaper than ours. Do not put more before an -er word: cheaper already means more cheap.

examples.en: This hotel room is cheaper than ours.
The shared bathroom is cleaner than before.
The train journey is shorter than ours.
The airport bus is slower than a taxi.
These leather shoes are softer than that pair.

fixes.wrong: This hotel room is more cheaper than ours.
fixes.right: This hotel room is cheaper than ours.

fixes.wrong: This hotel room is cheap than ours.
fixes.right: This hotel room is cheaper than ours.

fixes.wrong: The shared bathroom is cleaner that before.
fixes.right: The shared bathroom is cleaner than before.

blocks.text: When you choose one out of all of them, add -est and always put the before it: the shortest delivery time, the nearest shop. -er compares two things; the -est compares one with all the others.

examples.en: This shop has the shortest delivery time.
This clinic has the longest waiting time.
examples.translation: you wait longer here than anywhere

examples.en: This local shop is the nearest.
The plain yoghurt is the cheapest option.
We booked the earliest home visit.

fixes.wrong: This shop has shortest delivery time.
fixes.right: This shop has the shortest delivery time.

drill.question: You are looking at three shops. This one is bigger than both others. What do you say?
drill.optionA: This chain store is the larger.
drill.optionB: This chain store is the largest.

blocks.text: When there is no difference, put the describing word between two as: as strong as yours. The word stays plain, with no -er, and the second word is as, not than.

examples.en: This instant coffee is as strong as yours.
This green tea is as cheap as that one.
These reading glasses are as light as mine.
This electric kettle is as fast as ours.
examples.translation: it boils in the same time

fixes.wrong: This instant coffee is as stronger as yours.
fixes.right: This instant coffee is as strong as yours.

fixes.wrong: This instant coffee is as strong than yours.
fixes.right: This instant coffee is as strong as yours.

fixes.wrong: This ground coffee is fresh as yours.
fixes.right: This ground coffee is as fresh as yours.

blocks.text: too means more than is OK — a problem: This cabin bag is too big. enough means it is OK: This checked bag is light enough. too comes before the word; enough comes after it.

examples.en: This cabin bag is too big.
This checked bag is light enough.
The monthly rent is too high.
The rental deposit is low enough.
This driveway is too narrow.

fixes.wrong: This checked bag is enough light.
fixes.right: This checked bag is light enough.

fixes.wrong: This cabin bag is big too.
fixes.right: This cabin bag is too big.

drill.why: It is OK: enough, after the word.

sections.title: so and such — very, with feeling

blocks.text: With no thing after the describing word, use so: My close friend is so kind. When a thing follows, use such: such a helpful person, such hard work. The order is such a, not a such.

formula.text: with a thing: such a + word + thing

examples.en: My close friend is so kind.
Our mutual friend is such a helpful person.
This is such hard work.
The live music is so loud.
You have such a good memory.

fixes.wrong: Our mutual friend is so a helpful person.
fixes.right: Our mutual friend is such a helpful person.

fixes.wrong: My close friend is such kind.
fixes.right: My close friend is so kind.

fixes.wrong: Our mutual friend is a such helpful person.
fixes.right: Our mutual friend is such a helpful person.

drill.prompt: Say that your relationship is very good.

fixes.wrong: This hotel room is more cheaper than ours.
fixes.right: This hotel room is cheaper than ours.

fixes.wrong: This shop has shortest delivery time.
fixes.right: This shop has the shortest delivery time.

fixes.wrong: This instant coffee is as strong than yours.
fixes.right: This instant coffee is as strong as yours.

fixes.wrong: This checked bag is enough light.
fixes.right: This checked bag is light enough.

fixes.wrong: Our mutual friend is so a helpful person.
fixes.right: Our mutual friend is such a helpful person.

blocks.text: Two things — -er than. One out of all — the -est. The same — as … as. A problem — too before; OK — enough after. No thing — so; with a thing — such a.
-er than to compare two. the -est to choose one out of all. as … as for the same. too / enough for a problem or OK. so / such: so with no thing after, such with a thing.

examples.en: The sale price is lower than before.
This dining table is the widest.
This is such a big improvement.
examples.translation: a very big change for the better
